solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe bowler's in distress, with over not starting at all

indicators.note: in places the headwear inside the word for misery

parts.note: distress is woe
a bowler is one example of a hat, and the 's stays on as part of the word

indicators.note: not starting tells us to drop the opening letter of the word over

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler is struggling and the over has failed to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe bowler's' looks like cricket but a bowler is a hat; 'in' signals the container, and 'not starting' trims the second piece to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic phrases used after a negative: 'no doubt at all' means the same as 'no doubt whatever'.

clue.text: Half of sheep will arrive at Scottish town

indicators.note: half of says to keep only one of the two halves of the breed name

parts.note: the Herdwick is a hardy breed of sheep from the Lake District

explanation.surface: A flock of sheep, or part of one, is on its way to a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The sheep is the HERDWICK, a Lake District breed; take its second half. 'will arrive at' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Wick is a small town in Caithness on the far north-east coast of Scotland, an example of the category.

clue.text: Host cut short fuss about sick animal

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter of the word comes off

parts.note: a host is a great multitude, as in an army

indicators.note: about means the word for fuss goes around the other piece

parts.note: fuss is ado, as in much ado
sick is ill

explanation.surface: An abbreviated show of hospitality is spoilt by fussing over a poorly creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' suggests a party giver but means a multitude, as in a heavenly host; 'cut short' drops its last letter, and 'about' wraps the fuss round the sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas, a specific example of the general category.

clue.text: Criminal record, but no fine, after road rage

indicators.note: after puts the remaining record letters following the road abbreviation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, standing for road here

indicators.note: but no says the letter for fine is removed from the record

parts.note: form is slang for a criminal record
F stands for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A road-rage offender has previous convictions but escapes a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road rage' reads as one phrase; split it, with 'rage' as the definition. 'but no' strips the fine from the record, and 'after' puts the remainder behind the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Rage can mean a violent outburst, and a storm is used figuratively for such an outburst, as in a storm of anger.

clue.text: Go wrong with special assignments

parts.note: to err is to go wrong
with is and, joining things

explanation.surface: Special tasks have been botched.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are short trips or tasks someone is sent out to do, so they are small assignments.

clue.text: Green vines up the wall embodying Oxford University?

indicators.note: embodying means the jumbled letters hold the university abbreviation inside them
up the wall means driven crazy, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Climbing plants on a college wall make a picture of verdant Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green vines up the wall' reads as a garden scene; 'up the wall' rearranges the plants into ENVIS, and 'embodying' takes the university inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is the colour of jealousy, as in green with envy, so it means jealous or covetous.

clue.text: Wave misses small swimmer

indicators.note: misses means the word goes without the letter for small

parts.note: to shake is to wave, as a fist

explanation.surface: A wave fails to reach a small person swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: The hake is a fish of the cod family, and swimmer is a playful crossword term for any fish.

clue.text: Silver coin flipped for her

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: flipped means the coin word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: Someone tosses a silver coin to decide something for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' suggests tossing a coin but turns SEN to NES.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's given name, so it can stand for the pronoun as a particular female person.

clue.text: Extremely lean cuts for one and all

indicators.note: cuts means the pair of words slices into the abbreviation for example

parts.note: eg means for example, like for one
extremely means very
lean means thin

explanation.surface: A butcher offers very lean cuts to every customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lean cuts' looks like meat, but 'cuts' says the pair of words slices into the abbreviation for 'for one'.
explanation.definitionFit: All as a pronoun means every single thing, the whole lot, which is the same as the answer.

clue.text: Cherished religious gathering on 4th of March

indicators.note: gathering means the devout word gathers in the other letters

parts.note: religious means pious
re means on, concerning

indicators.note: 4th of picks the fourth letter of the month name

explanation.surface: A cherished church gathering takes place on the fourth of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious gathering' reads as a service, but 'religious' is the outer word and 'gathering' takes in 'on' plus C, the 4th letter of March.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious describes something greatly loved and valued, a close synonym of treasured.

clue.text: Short literary piece is a gem

definitions.meaning: a brief descriptive sketch in writing
a stone carved in relief, set in jewellery

explanation.surface: A brief piece of writing is praised as a little treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is both a short vivid character sketch in writing and a carved stone with a raised design.

clue.text: Respect, veneration principally for fellow?

indicators.note: for means the leading letter goes in place of the letter for fellow

parts.note: in respect of means with reference to

indicators.note: principally means taking the first letter of the word veneration

explanation.surface: Respect and veneration are what a learned fellow chiefly expects.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: REFERENCE (respect) has V for F; the whole clue also defines the answer, since 'Your Reverence' is a title for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverence is deep respect and veneration, and the question mark hints at its use as a title for a clergyman.

clue.text: One female embracing chaps with love for Mozart opera

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: embracing means the female word wraps round the word for chaps

parts.note: a doe is a female deer or rabbit
chaps are men
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A single woman surrounded by admirers is in love at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts the chaps inside the female deer; love is the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Idomeneo, re di Creta is an opera seria by Mozart first staged in Munich in 1781.

clue.text: Soft copper has a fling

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to shy is to fling or throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A soft-hearted police officer is having an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' and 'fling' suggest a policeman's affair; the copper is the metal and a fling is a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is soft or easy, needing little effort; both are informal ways to describe a comfortable number.

clue.text: Rock gig's as ever in-your-face

indicators.note: rock means to shake about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rock concert is confrontational as always.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock gig' reads as one concert, but 'Rock' shakes up GIGSASEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: In-your-face describes confrontational, pushy behaviour, much like hostile and forceful conduct.

clue.text: Government permits on which one could get hung up?

definitions.text: on which one could get hung up?

parts.note: permits means allows

explanation.surface: The authorities sanction something that might make a person fixated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hung up' suggests being obsessed; here it means hanged on a scaffold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is the frame used for hanging people, so a person could be literally strung up on it.

clue.text: Look up lines supporting new gold standard in America

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the lines come underneath
up in a down clue means the word for look reads backwards

parts.note: lo means look, as in lo and behold

indicators.note: new means the metal word is made afresh in a new order

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Fresh gold backed by lines suggests the gold standard of the US economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold standard' reads as finance, but 'standard' means a flag; 'up' turns LO to OL, 'new' makes DGLO of GOLD, 'supporting' puts RY below.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname of the United States flag, and a standard is a flag or banner.

clue.text: Bear is shot, sadly, to get hold of coat

indicators.note: to get hold of means the jumbled letters grasp the coat word inside
sadly signals the word shot is badly arranged

parts.note: taken as written
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: A bear has been shot, and sadly someone wants its fur as a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb, to tolerate. 'sadly' reorders the shot to STOH and 'to get hold of' puts the raincoat inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it, the verb sense of endure.

clue.text: An inventor such as Noah?

definitions.meaning: Richard ... invented the water-powered spinning frame in the 18th century
a wright is a builder, and Noah built the ark

explanation.surface: Noah is held up as an early inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Wright means a maker, as in shipwright, so a builder of an ark is an ark-wright.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright pioneered the factory spinning frame, and the name splits into a maker of an ark.

clue.text: Charlie ignored part-time judge's request again

indicators.note: ignored means the letter for Charlie is left out of the word

parts.note: a recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge in England
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie paid no heed when a judge asked for something a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: A RECORDER is a part-time judge in English courts; the 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder means to place a further order for goods, which is to ask for them a second time.

clue.text: Update whistleblower before she runs off

indicators.note: before puts the official first, ahead of the other letters

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, and ref is short for referee
R stands for runs in cricket scoring

indicators.note: off means these letters go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whistleblower gives an update before the woman flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistleblower' suggests an informant but is the referee; 'off' rearranges SHE with R (runs) to give RESH.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh a web page or display is to bring it up to date, a computing sense of renew.

clue.text: Writer wants to encourage relations

parts.note: to push someone is to encourage or urge them on
kin are relations

explanation.surface: An author is keen to cheer on the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pushkin was the great Russian poet and novelist, author of Eugene Onegin.

clue.text: First of phones needing modern charger

indicators.note: First of picks the opening letter of the word phones

parts.note: latter means more recent, nearer to the present

explanation.surface: A modern phone needs a new charger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charger' looks like a phone charger but is an old word for a large serving dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a large flat dish, the same kind of serving dish as a platter.

clue.text: Quiet one bores Afghan?

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
an awl is a tool that bores holes

explanation.surface: A quiet man from Afghanistan is said to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afghan' looks like a person or a dog, but an afghan is also a knitted blanket or wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: An afghan is a knitted or crocheted woollen blanket or wrap, worn round the shoulders like a stole.

clue.text: Liberal politician gets stuck into beer

indicators.note: gets stuck into means the politician goes inside the drink word

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat MP gets stuck into a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal politician' reads as a party member; 'Liberal' is the definition, meaning generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, which is a synonym of abundant.

clue.text: Sugar in coffee? Cook assumes that

indicators.note: assumes means the cooking word takes on the coffee word within it

parts.note: to fry is to cook
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: Someone takes sugar in their coffee, and the cook takes that for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar in coffee' looks like one phrase; 'Sugar' alone is the definition, and 'that' points back to the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar here means sweet talk, insincere praise used to win someone over.

clue.text: Put forward bill legislature voided

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: voided means the middle of the word legislature is emptied out

explanation.surface: A proposed bill is thrown out by parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voided' suggests a law annulled; it empties LEGISLATURE to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To table a motion, in British usage, is to propose it for discussion.

clue.text: Not all fancy a neutral colour

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone likes a neutral shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue shade, one of the primary inks in colour printing.

clue.text: Nursing cold, lost temper if tense

indicators.note: nursing means the jumbled letters hold the cold letter inside them
lost means the letters are confused and rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone nursing a cold loses their temper if they get tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervy but is the grammatical tense; 'lost' reorders TEMPERIF to IMPERFET and 'Nursing' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is a grammatical tense for continuous or repeated past action, as in 'I was walking'.

clue.text: Faulty goods included in purchase

indicators.note: included in means the goods letters go inside the purchase word

parts.note: a purchase is a buy
G is short for good, so two goods are GG

explanation.surface: Defective goods turned up in what someone bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Software full of errors is described as buggy, meaning it has faults or defects.

clue.text: Still calm (just) with scores level

definitions.meaning: used before a comparative, as in more so
placid and steady, as of temper
fair and equal, as in an ...-handed deal

explanation.surface: A tense match is still calm, just about, with the scores tied.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions in a row: the word means each of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an intensifier ('better still'), as placid, as fair, and as tied in a contest.

clue.text: She does spill the beans about Society dance

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, one who does for her employer

indicators.note: about means the revealing phrase goes around the society letter

parts.note: to let on is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A woman gives away a secret about a society ball.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR (charwoman) is a British cleaner who 'does' a house; 'about' wraps LET ON around S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s jazz dance named after the city in South Carolina.
